subject: NebulaWorks renewal — capacity add & throughput guarantee request
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Chen <ari@nebulaworks.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal conversation: forecast + preliminary capacity ask

Hi Ari —

Quick note to kick off the renewal planning for NebulaWorks. Thanks again for the usage data you shared last quarter — we modeled trend lines against your Q4 spike and the new feature rollout you mentioned. Attached is a first-pass forecast (qps_forecast_v1.xlsx) showing expected steady growth and a 2x burst risk window during product releases.

High-level ask from our side: based on your current mix (short-chat + long-gen windowed at ~1.2k tokens/session) we recommend provisioning an additional reserved pool of 8 NVIDIA A100-equivalent GPUs to support the forecasted 45% QPS growth through the contract year with a 15% headroom for bursts. This keeps average P99 latency under your 300ms SLO for chat endpoints and preserves cost predictability.

Can we schedule a 30-min alignment this week to walk the numbers and firm up the term change (12 -> 18 months) and throughput guarantee? Proposed times: Fri 2/13 9:30–10:00 PT or Mon 2/16 11:00–11:30 PT.

Attaching: qps_forecast_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Ben Carter

Ben —

Thanks for the model and the quick turnaround. A couple quick clarifications before the meeting:
- Can you break the forecast into chat vs. long-gen token mix? Our cost center needs to see token-weighted view.
- We currently have a temporary spike pattern tied to nightly batch jobs (approx 2x baseline for ~30 minutes). Will the reserved pool recommendation assume automatic bursting, or do we need separate burst credits?

We can do Fri 9:30 PT. Adding Sam (ops) — he will want to confirm VPC & private deployment constraints.

Best,

On Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 1:23 PM Ari Chen <ari@nebulaworks.ai> wrote:
> Ben —
>
> Thanks for the model and the quick turnaround. A couple quick clarifications before the meeting:
> - Can you break the forecast into chat vs. long-gen token mix? Our cost center needs to see token-weighted view.
> - We currently have a temporary spike pattern tied to nightly batch jobs (approx 2x baseline for ~30 minutes). Will the reserved pool recommendation assume automatic bursting, or do we need separate burst credits?

Thanks — good questions. Short answers below and we'll walk the sheet on the call: 
- I attached an updated tab in the drive (linked in the thread) that slices chat vs. long-gen by Q1/Q2. Chat sessions drive the bulk of QPS; long-gen consumes more tokens per request. We show token-weighted units in column F.
- The 8-GPU reserved pool recommendation assumes we provision a dedicated pool for your account that can take sustained QPS increases. For the nightly 2x spike we recommend combining the reserved pool with 2 instances of burst capacity (on-demand burst credits) to avoid overcommit while keeping predictable monthly commit. If you prefer, we can size the reserved pool up by +2 GPUs instead and reduce burst credits — tradeoff is commit cost vs. burst fee.

Proposed on-call agenda (15–20 min):
- Review chat vs long-gen split and token-weighted forecast (Monica)
- Confirm target P99 latency & throughput guarantee (Marissa)
- Confirm deployment (Dedicated reserved pool in us-west-2 + VPC peering)

See you Fri 9:30 PT.

Ben

--
Monica Patel

Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Renewal conversation: forecast + preliminary capacity ask

Thanks all — good cadence. A couple procurement/ops notes we should capture before the term is final:
- NebulaWorks has requested an 18-month term with a throughput SLA at P99 <= 300ms for chat endpoints and an uptime SLA of 99.9% for the dedicated pool. Ops can accept 99.9% if we include a Tiered credit schedule (detailed in SOW).
- I drafted a one-page SOW and uploaded SOW-draft-NebulaWorks.pdf to the drive. Key items: reserved pool size (8 GPUs), optional +2 GPU buffer for burst vs burst credits, on-call escalation path, and rollback policy for model fallback to a smaller variant.
- Procurement will need the finalized token-weighted forecast (Monica — please add a tab with month-by-month committed tokens and estimated overage rates).

I'll loop Rishi for final approval on the pricing uplift once the forecast and SOW are updated.

Marissa Cole
Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Next steps & confirmation: NebulaWorks renewal capacity add

Ari / Sam —

Thanks for the productive conversation earlier. To summarize the proposed renewal expansion so procurement and engineering can move forward: 
1) Term: 18 months (start: 2026-03-01)
2) Reserved pool: 8 NVIDIA A100-equivalent GPUs in us-west-2 (dedicated to NebulaWorks)
3) Burst strategy: +2 on-demand burst credits for nightly spikes (or option to convert to +2 reserved GPUs for a 9% additional commit cost)
4) Throughput guarantee: P99 latency <= 300ms for chat endpoints; SOW includes credit schedule for SLA miss events
5) Token-weighted commit: monthly committed token units (see updated forecast link). Overages billed at negotiated rates in SOW.
6) Rollout plan: canary 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over 72 hours; rollback policy documented in SOW.

Action items:
- Ben: send finalized SOW (DocuSign link) for signature and attach the month-by-month committed tokens.
- Monica: upload the token-weighted forecast tab and confirm estimated monthly overage at the agreed rate.
- Ari: confirm whether NebulaWorks prefers burst credits or the +2 reserved GPUs option by EOD Fri 2/20.
